newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Under a decision designed to keep wages growth within the Reserve Bank of Australia's inflation target, the Australian Industrial Relations Commission has granted workers who rely on award pay rates a A$10-a-week pay rise, setting a new Federal minimum award wage of A$359.40 a week. Page 1.

Thanks largely to the A$3 billion special dividend from Telstra and higher returns on airport privatisation, the Federal Government is expecting to save around A$700 million in public debt interest outlays, reducing its underlying Budget deficit over the ext two years. Page 3.

Although Federal Cabinet decided yesterday to offer the Radio Australia service a reprieve, albeit cutting its present funding of A$23 million down to A$7.2 million, the Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission and the Law Reform Commission are set t take fresh cuts in the upcoming Budget. Page 5.

In a move putting him at odds with Federal colleagues, Queensland's National Party Premier Rob Borbidge has refused any compromise on native title, saying he will accept nothing short of total legislative extinguishment of native title over leasehold landand reject Prime Minister John Howard's 10-point plan on the issue, which Borbidge says would "stuff the bush". Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In what the Federal Government has described as a blow to the ACTU's credibility, the Industrial Relations Commission yesterday rejected the ACTU's "living wage" claim as inflationary and a threat to low interest rates, delivering a A$10-a-week pay rise fr up to two million employees and set a new Federal minimum wage. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard announced his support for Opposition frontbencher Carmen Lawrence yesterday, saying she was entitled to a presumption of innocence regarding perjury charges arising from her evidence to the Easton royal commission in 1995 and tht she has the right to remain in Parliament while she faces court over the charges. Page 1.

According to an analysis of Newspoll results following the launch of Pauline Hanson's One Nation party in Queensland 12 days ago, the controversial party has the same voter support as the Australian Democrats, placing it within reach of Senate seats in Quensland and New South Wales if Prime Minister John Howard opted for a double dissolution election. Page 1.

Under a Cabinet compromise yesterday that would slash Radio Australia's A$20.5 million a year budget by about A$13 million, the service would be able to continue its English-language short-wave service to Papua New Guinea and the Pacific, but would drop mst of its services to Asia, including Asian-language services to countries like China. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto is expected to fight to secure a more influential role for Australia in the Asian region, including early membership of the Asia Europe Meeting (ASEM) which Malaysia has blocked Australia from joining, when he mees with Prime Minister John Howard in Canberra on Monday. Page 1.

In a six-to-one majority yesterday, the National Wage Bench of the Industrial Relations Commission heeded Reserve Bank warnings that the ACTU's living wage claim would bring a rise in interest rates and ruled that workers unable to strike a wage bargain wth their employers will get a A$10-a-week pay rise. Page 1.

Former Victorian premier Joan Kirner is leading a force of senior female ALP members to support former West Australian Premier Carmen Lawrence. Kirner said yesterday the perjury charges against Lawrence were the end result of what amounted to a "politica witch-hunt". Page 1.

In an unusual move, Australian media magnate Kerry Packer has travelled to Canberra to meet with Prime Minister John Howard to persuade Howard to change cross-media rules so he can takeover the Fairfax newspaper group. Packer warned that unless Fairfax ha a sufficient financial base, it would be destroyed by on-line services run by multi-national competitors. Page 1.
THE AGE

In a blow to the ACTU, the Australian Industrial Relations Commission released its long-awaited living wage decision yesterday, which allocated an extra A$10-a-week to the 1.7 million workers covered by minimum-rates Federal awards. The decision will see housands of employees, mainly in the pastoral, agricultural, hospitality and retail industries, receiving pay rises of up to A$100-a-week. Page 1.

Just a week after a 25-year-old policeman from Melbourne was dismissed for failing to stop after an accident in 1996, an off-duty officer allegedly recorded a blood-alcohol reading almost three times the legal limit early yesterday after crashing a speed amera car into a passenger vehicle carrying two children. It is believed the policeman drove away from the accident without stopping. Page 1.

Under a compromise Expenditure Review Committee proposal accepted by Federal Cabinet, the ABC's Radio Australia service will see its budget slashed by two thirds and many of its operations dumped. Under the offer, the service will effectively be reduced t operating in the Papua New Guinea and the Pacific region as Chinese and South-East Asian services are scrapped. Page 1.

Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto is expected to pledge strong support for the "institutionalisation" of Australia's presence in Asia when he meets Australian Prime Minister John Howard next week. Hashimoto is scheduled to present an 18-point blueprint for Australia's increased role, covering areas such as trade, science, education and medical research. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
